stats_check_nc_run: Check the numbers in my document
stats_check_text_gone: That text is not in the document any more. Scan again.
stats_check_text_nowhere: Open your document in the writing window to go to this text.
stats_check_rt_desc: Every result you insert from the Data tab carries a hidden tag that remembers which test it came from and which data it was run on. This list reads every document in this project and compares each tagged result with the latest data stored under the same data set name. A result marked out of date was run on data that has since changed.
stats_check_rt_locked: Your vault is locked. Unlock it to compare results with your data.
stats_check_rt_unreadable: Your saved results or data sets could not be read, so nothing can be compared.
stats_check_rt_none: No tagged results found in the documents of this project. If your vault is locked, unlock it and scan again. Results inserted from the Data tab are tagged.
stats_check_rt_readonly: Re-running changes your documents, so it works in the writing window.
stats_check_why_noset: The data set “{n}” has no record in this project, so there is nothing to compare with. Paste it in the Data tab under the same name and press Parse data.
stats_check_load_first: Load the changed data first: paste it in the Data tab, name it “{n}” and press Parse data.
stats_check_gone: This sentence is no longer in the document. Scan again.
stats_check_nowrite: “{title}” could not be changed: it was deleted, or it holds text that has not been saved yet. Nothing was replaced.
stats_check_all_summary: Updated {done} of {n} out-of-date results. {skipped} skipped, {failed} could not be re-run.
stats_data_privacy: Paste a table from Excel, SPSS, Google Sheets or a CSV file, with the column names in the first row. Your rows are not sent or saved anywhere: they stay in memory and are gone when you reload or close the page. Only the data set's name, its row count and a fingerprint of it are saved to your project.
stats_data_name_help: This name is saved with your project, with the row count and a fingerprint of the data, so a later version of the data under the same name can be told apart.
stats_data_empty: Paste some data first: one row of column names, then your rows.
stats_data_read_failed: That file could not be read. Save it as .csv and try again.
stats_data_split_done: Data split on semicolons and parsed.
stats_data_busy: Reading your data. This takes a moment for a large table.
stats_data_skipped: Rows left out: {n}. Each has a different number of values than the first row. Lines in your paste: {lines}.
stats_data_semicolon: The first row has semicolons but no commas or tabs, so it was read as one column. If your values are separated by semicolons, split them.
stats_data_sets_confirm: Your saved list of data sets cannot be opened on this device. Saving now replaces it. Save anyway?
stats_pd_intro: Choose what to do with each column. Removing is safest. A code keeps rows linked to one person without showing who, and you get a key file that maps each code back.
stats_pd_select_aria: What to do with the column {name}
stats_pd_label_roll: looks like roll or enrolment numbers
stats_pd_label_address: looks like an address or place
stats_pd_label_govid: looks like a government ID number
stats_pd_pseudo: A code is pseudonymisation, not anonymisation. While the key file exists, the data still counts as personal data. Keep the key file away from the data, for example on a different drive, and share only the coded data. If you lose the key file, nobody can recover the names.
stats_pd_scope: This check reads column headings and the shape of the values. It cannot see a name typed inside an open answer. Read those yourself before they go anywhere.
stats_pd_none: Checked the column headings and the values for names, phone numbers, email addresses, roll or enrolment numbers, dates of birth, addresses and government ID numbers. No column was flagged.
stats_pd_unchanged: Nothing changed. You chose to keep every flagged column.
stats_pd_keyed: The key file was downloaded. Store it apart from the data.
stats_run_need_data: Parse your data first. The tests appear here once there is a table.
stats_run_practice: Practice mode: commit to my design before the test runs
stats_run_footer: These formulas cover the common cases correctly (Welch's independent t, average-rank non-parametric tests, standard ANOVA and chi-square). For an unusual design, or before a dissertation defense, cross-check against SPSS or JASP.
stats_gate_question: Before it runs: what is your design?
stats_gate_switched: Switched. Choose your columns, then check again.
stats_res_explain_label: Written by AI. Check it against the table above before you use it.
stats_res_explain_failed: The explanation could not be made. Try again.
stats_res_runs_confirm: Your saved list of inserted results cannot be opened on this device. Saving now replaces it. Save anyway? If you cancel, the sentence is still inserted, without a link back to its data.
stats_chart_interaction: Interaction plot: mean {dv} by {a}, one line per {b} (parallel lines mean no interaction)
stats_chart_slopes: Simple slopes: {y} on {x} at three levels of {w}
stats_res_copy_failed: Could not copy. Select the text instead.
stats_guide_intro: Answer a few plain questions. The guide suggests a test, says why it fits, and offers a small practice example.
stats_guide_chosen: {name} is chosen in Run a test, below.
stats_guide_need_data: Paste and parse your data first, then tap Use this test.
stats_guide_unbuilt: The app does not run this test yet. This is a case for a human or a statistician to confirm, and the app will hand it over once the full workflow is built. Until then, run it in jamovi or JASP (both free) and bring the numbers back here to write up.
stats_guide_demo_invented: The numbers are invented for practice.
stats_guide_predict_ask: Before you run it, what do you expect?
stats_guide_demo_run: Run the demo in the Stats Lab
stats_guide_demo_need_pred: Make your prediction first, then run the demo.
stats_guide_says_clear: The test says there was a clear result.
stats_guide_says_none: The test says there was no clear result.
stats_guide_scale: Here is what the scale did.
stats_guide_demo_apart: This is practice data. Your own data, results and sentences are as you left them, and nothing from the demo is saved or put into your document.
stats_guide_check_help: Group sizes, skew and outliers for a score, and expected counts for two categories. Shown as information. Nothing here blocks a test.
stats_guide_check_need: Parse your data first and this box will check group sizes, skew, outliers and expected counts.
stats_guide_check_not_proof: This looked only at group size, skew, outliers and expected counts. It does not show that the test's assumptions are met.
stats_power_intro: How many people does the study need, how much power does a given sample have, or what is the smallest effect a given sample can detect. Everything is computed here from the exact noncentral distributions; nothing is uploaded.
stats_power_test_chisq: Chi-square test (table or goodness of fit)
stats_power_solve_effect: The smallest effect my sample can detect
stats_power_df: Degrees of freedom of the table
stats_power_benchmarks: Cohen's benchmarks for {sym} are {list} (small, medium, large). They are a last resort. Better is the smallest effect you would care about, or an effect taken from earlier studies, kept on the cautious side.
stats_power_sim_intro: Run a few hundred pretend studies of the same size on a computer and see how many of them find a real effect. Everything here is SIMULATED. No real people, no data file, and nothing here can be copied into a study. It exists to show why a small study misses real effects and why the studies that do find it overstate it.
stats_power_sim_setup: Two groups of equal size. The true difference between them is the effect size d you choose. Each pretend study draws new people and runs an independent-samples t-test at alpha .05, two-tailed.
stats_ch_studio_intro: Paste your data with the column names in the first row, or use the table you parsed in the Data tab. Pick a chart. Every chart is drawn on this computer, and you can put it in your paper.
stats_ch_use_lab: Use the data from the Data tab
stats_ch_no_lab: Nothing is parsed in the Data tab yet. Parse a table there first, or paste it here.
stats_ch_from_lab: Drawing from the table in the Data tab ({n} rows).
stats_ch_no_columns: No columns could be read from this. Put the column names in the first row.
stats_ch_failed: This chart could not be drawn from these group names. Rename the group (a name such as constructor or toString cannot be used) and try again.
stats_ch_quick_intro: Make a bar or line chart from your own numbers, or a Venn diagram, then insert it into your document as a picture.
stats_ch_q_empty: Add at least one "label,value" line first.
stats_sc_intro: Published scales with the owner's own wording. The text is fixed and never rewritten by the AI, because a reworded item is no longer the validated item. Each scale shows its licence record. Check that the terms fit your use before you put a scale in a study.
stats_sc_credit: Credit line to print with the scale: {credit}
stats_sc_score: Score this scale in my data
stats_sc_score_intro: Match each item to its column. Items that need reverse-scoring are handled for you. Give the data as the raw answers, not already reversed.
stats_sc_coding: How are your answers coded in the data?
stats_sc_run: Compute scores and add them to my data
stats_sc_nodata: Parse data on the Data tab first. The scores are added to that table.
stats_sc_pd_again: The table was checked for personal details again with the new columns. Some columns were flagged: review them on the Data tab before you share or save this data.
